text: Batch normalization normalizes the activations of a layer using the mean and variance of the current mini-batch. It was introduced in 2015 and typically allows learning rates up to 10 times larger. At inference time it uses running averages collected during training instead of batch statistics. A common side effect is a mild regularization effect.
title: Batch normalization

text: Dropout randomly sets a fraction of the activations to zero during training, commonly 0.5 for fully connected layers. At test time all units are active and the outputs are scaled accordingly. The technique reduces co-adaptation between neurons and is a cheap form of regularization. Dropout is usually not applied to the output layer.
title: Dropout

text: Adam combines momentum with per-parameter adaptive learning rates. It keeps exponential moving averages of the gradient and of its square, with default decay rates of 0.9 and 0.999. A small constant of 1e-8 is added to the denominator for numerical stability. AdamW decouples weight decay from the gradient update.
title: Adam optimizer

text: Learning rate warmup increases the learning rate linearly from a small value over the first steps of training. Transformers are often trained with a warmup of several thousand steps followed by a decay. Without warmup, large models can diverge early because the optimizer statistics are still unreliable.
title: Learning rate warmup

text: Byte pair encoding builds a subword vocabulary by repeatedly merging the most frequent pair of adjacent symbols. A vocabulary of 32,000 merges is typical for translation systems. Rare words are split into pieces, so the model never meets an unknown token. Byte-level variants start from the 256 possible bytes.
title: Byte pair encoding

text: BERT is an encoder-only Transformer pre-trained with masked language modelling. About 15 percent of the input tokens are masked and the model predicts them from both directions. The base model has 12 layers and 110 million parameters, while the large model has 24 layers and 340 million parameters.
title: BERT

text: GPT models are decoder-only Transformers trained to predict the next token. A causal mask prevents each position from attending to later positions. Generation proceeds one token at a time, which makes inference sequential even though training is parallel.
title: GPT models

text: Word2vec learns word embeddings by predicting words from their context. The skip-gram variant predicts the surrounding words from the centre word, while CBOW predicts the centre word from its context. Negative sampling replaces the full softmax with a handful of random negative examples, which makes training fast.
title: Word2vec

text: TF-IDF weights a term by its frequency in a document multiplied by the logarithm of the inverse document frequency. Terms that occur in almost every document receive weights close to zero. The method ignores word order and is a classic baseline for document retrieval.
title: TF-IDF

text: BM25 refines TF-IDF with term frequency saturation and document length normalization. The parameter k1 controls saturation and is often set between 1.2 and 2.0. The parameter b controls length normalization and is commonly 0.75. BM25 remains a strong baseline for retrieval.
title: BM25

text: A cross-encoder reads the query and a passage together in a single Transformer pass and outputs a relevance score. It is more accurate than a bi-encoder but far slower, because nothing can be precomputed. Rerankers are therefore applied only to the top 20 to 100 candidates returned by a first-stage retriever.
title: Cross-encoder reranking

text: A bi-encoder embeds queries and documents independently, so document vectors can be computed once and stored in an index. Relevance is the cosine similarity between the two vectors. Sentence-BERT popularised this design, which scales to millions of documents with approximate nearest-neighbour search.
title: Bi-encoder retrieval

text: Hierarchical navigable small world graphs organise vectors in layers of proximity graphs. A search starts in the sparse top layer and descends to the dense bottom layer. The parameter efSearch trades recall for speed. HNSW offers high recall but needs the whole graph in memory.
title: HNSW index

text: Knowledge distillation trains a small student model to imitate a larger teacher. The student learns from the teacher's output probabilities, softened with a temperature, which carry more information than hard labels. DistilBERT keeps about 97 percent of the language understanding performance of BERT with 40 percent fewer parameters.
title: Knowledge distillation

text: In k-fold cross-validation the data is split into k parts, and each part serves once as the validation set. A common choice is k equal to 5 or 10. Stratified folds keep the class proportions identical in every fold. Cross-validation gives a more stable estimate than a single split but costs k training runs.
title: Cross-validation

text: Precision is the share of predicted positives that are correct, and recall is the share of actual positives that are found. The F1 score is their harmonic mean. On imbalanced data, accuracy can be misleading because a model that always predicts the majority class scores high.
title: Precision and recall

text: A model is calibrated when its predicted probabilities match observed frequencies: among predictions with 80 percent confidence, about 80 percent are correct. Expected calibration error summarises the gap over confidence bins. Temperature scaling divides the logits by a single learned scalar and is a simple post-hoc fix.
title: Calibration

text: Data leakage happens when information from the test set influences training, for example by fitting a scaler on all the data before splitting. It inflates evaluation scores and gives a false sense of progress. Time series need splits that respect chronological order.
title: Data leakage

text: Transfer learning reuses a network pre-trained on a large dataset such as ImageNet. Only the last layers are replaced and trained on the new task, or the whole network is fine-tuned with a small learning rate. It works well when labelled data is scarce.
title: Transfer learning

text: Mixed precision training keeps a master copy of the weights in 32-bit floats but computes the forward and backward passes in 16-bit. Loss scaling avoids gradient underflow. On recent GPUs it can roughly double throughput and halves activation memory.
title: Mixed precision training

text: In quantum chemistry, quantization of the vibrational energy levels of a molecule means that only discrete energies are allowed. Spectroscopy measures transitions between these levels. The spacing depends on the bond strength and the masses of the atoms.
title: Quantization in chemistry

text: Post-training quantization converts the weights of a trained model from 32-bit floats to 8-bit integers, shrinking the model size by about 4 times. Quantization-aware training simulates the rounding during training and usually loses less accuracy. Integer arithmetic also speeds up inference on CPUs.
title: Model quantization

text: Self-attention compares every token with every other token, so its memory and compute grow quadratically with the sequence length. For a sequence of 4,096 tokens the attention matrix has about 16.8 million entries per head. Sparse and linear attention variants reduce this cost.
title: Attention complexity

text:
Early stopping halts training when the validation loss has not improved for a number of epochs called the patience. It acts as a regularizer and saves compute. The best checkpoint is restored at the end, so the final model is the one with the lowest validation loss. Practitioners usually monitor the same metric they report at the end of the project.

References

[1] Prechelt, L. (1998). Early stopping - but when? In Neural Networks: Tricks of the Trade, pages 55-69. Springer.
[2] Goodfellow, I., Bengio, Y., Courville, A. (2016). Deep Learning. MIT Press, Cambridge, MA.
title: Early stopping

text: L2 regularization adds the sum of squared weights to the loss, which shrinks weights toward zero. L1 regularization adds the sum of absolute values and tends to produce sparse solutions. The regularization strength is a hyperparameter usually chosen by validation.
title: Weight regularization
